hero.label: Doubao for Work Integration
hero.title: Bring RedNote & Douyin data into Doubao for Work: one connector, one research skill
hero.description: MediaClaw gives Doubao for Work two things: a RedNote (Xiaohongshu) and Douyin MCP server whose 40+ tools collect posts, videos, comments and account data and dedupe them into structured results, and a content research skill whose 12 written methods handle teardowns, topic picks and drafting. The only difference from Codex and WorkBuddy is the install: Doubao for Work needs you to save a local STDIO connector by hand under Skills · Connectors · Partners, and the agent itself prepares every field you have to fill in. After that, describe the goal in plain language.
hero.tip: You need the MediaClaw browser extension installed and an active membership first. Set the connector up on the same computer that runs the extension. The agent can only use capabilities you approved in the extension, and every page visit still happens in your own browser.

tasks.title: What one sentence gets you once Doubao for Work is connected
tasks.description: All six are real MediaClaw Agent runs. The prompts are copy-ready — swap what's in angle brackets for your own. Every host runs the same MCP tools and the same methods, so the output is identical; the chat window in these screenshots may not match yours, but what comes back does.

items.title: See who is winning: top posts ranked by likes
items.description: “Show me the top RedNote posts on <keyword> from the last six months and rank the representative ones by likes.” It organizes the sample it just collected and charts like counts, so which content actually earned engagement is visible at a glance.

image.alt: Doubao for Work charting the like counts of collected RedNote posts on a keyword

items.title: Then pick a direction: turn the sample into topics you can write
items.description: Ask it to group the same sample by content direction, list representative posts for each, and suggest topics worth trying. Want to go deeper on one? Have it back-fill the body text and comments of those posts. The ranking and conclusions come from that sample, so they shift with the keyword and time range.

image.alt: Doubao for Work grouping collected posts into topic directions with suggested ideas

items.title: Mine a comment section for topics you can write
items.description: “Pull at least 300 comments from this post, analyse what readers want, and tell me which topics I can take.” 322 comments deduped to 280, 35.4% of them explicit needs, delivered as a prioritized topic list and a multi-sheet workbook.

image.alt: Turning collected RedNote comments into a ranked topic list and a multi-sheet workbook

items.title: See what a topic looks like across both platforms
items.description: “Check what new techniques people are posting about <keyword> on RedNote and Douyin lately.” It pins down which product the keyword means, reuses the existing RedNote sample, back-fills only Douyin, and groups recent patterns into 7 categories with examples.

image.alt: Cross-platform topic research grouping recent patterns into seven categories

items.title: Today's posts only — no last month's hits
items.description: “Show me RedNote posts about <keyword> published today.” 80 latest posts scanned as of 23:48, grouped by content direction with the current top performers listed. Run it daily and it becomes lightweight monitoring.

image.alt: Pulling the day's newest RedNote posts and grouping them by direction

items.title: Tear down a video, then get a script you can shoot
items.description: “Why does this video keep people watching? How does the opening land and how does it build? Also turn it into a script I can shoot.” A precise teardown needs the transcript, so it quotes first (16 credits / 40 balance / an expiry), extracts only after you confirm, then returns the structure plus a 90-second script.

image.alt: Extracting a video's structure and handing back a shoot-ready 90-second script

setup.title: Getting connected: four steps to one local connector
setup.description: Doubao for Work has no automatic install entry yet, so you save the connector by hand. You do not have to work out what goes in it: the agent prepares the runtime files first, then hands you a list with the server name, transport, command, arguments and environment variables. Do this on the same computer that runs the MediaClaw extension, with the browser and extension open.

items.title: Step 1: Copy the Doubao install prompt from the extension
items.description: Open System settings → Agent access in the extension, turn on “Allow local agents to call MediaClaw”, expand “Connect Agent”, and hit Copy on the Doubao for Work row. Make sure you take that row — its prompt differs from the Codex and WorkBuddy ones.

image.alt: MediaClaw's Agent access panel: enabling local agent calls and copying the install prompt

items.title: Step 2: Send it to Doubao and let it produce the configuration list
items.description: Start a task in Doubao for Work and paste the prompt as-is. It prepares the runtime files, then lists the server name, transport, command, arguments and environment variables. That list is generated for your machine — keep it for the next step, and never copy paths out of a screenshot.

image.alt: Doubao for Work generating the MediaClaw connector configuration for the current computer

items.title: Step 3: Create the custom connector, fill it in and switch it on
items.description: Open Skills · Connectors · Partners in the sidebar, then New → New custom connector. Name the server mediaclaw, pick STDIO as the transport, copy the command and arguments from the list, and add the environment variables one row per pair. Save, wait for “Connector installed”, then check under My skills → Connectors that its toggle is on.

image.alt: Filling the Doubao for Work custom connector with the command, arguments and environment variables

items.title: Step 4: Approve the pairing, then verify back in Doubao
items.description: A pending device appears in the extension's Agent access tab. Check that it is Doubao for Work and that the fingerprint matches the one Doubao showed you, then hit Approve — a green “Agent connected” banner does not count while a device is still pending. Back in Doubao, say “the connector is created and the extension approved the pairing, please re-check the connection”; it verifies with a real tool call and shows the welcome message.

image.alt: Verifying the Doubao for Work device fingerprint and approving the pairing in MediaClaw

items.question: Why does Doubao for Work need an extra connector step?
items.answer: Codex and WorkBuddy have their own plugin managers, so the agent can install the package and register the tools end to end. Doubao for Work currently needs you to save a custom connector in its UI, which tells it where to launch the local MediaClaw tools from and how to connect to them. The install prompt makes Doubao prepare the runtime files and turn the required fields into a list — you just copy it across once.

items.question: Do I have to write the command and paths myself?
items.answer: No. The list is generated for your machine; copy it item by item. Two things to watch: if an argument is marked as blank, do not click Add and do not literally type “blank”; and the documentation screenshots use a local development setup, so their command paths, Node path and local markers are UI examples only — never copy them.

items.question: I saved it, but Doubao still cannot call the tools.
items.answer: Check three things in order. One: under My skills → Connectors, is the MediaClaw toggle on? Two: does the extension's Agent access tab still show a pending device — a green “Agent connected” banner does not count while one is waiting. Three: are the browser and extension running on the same computer as the connector? If all three are fine, ask Doubao to re-check the connection and it will verify with a real tool call.

items.question: Can Doubao for Work auto-update?
items.answer: No. On Codex and WorkBuddy you can say “upgrade MediaClaw Agent” in an existing conversation and the agent handles it. Doubao for Work has no automatic install entry, so after a new extension release you redo the install and connector configuration by hand. Either way you must fully quit and reopen the host — a running process will not hot-load a new version.

items.question: Does driving it from Doubao burn a lot of tokens?
items.answer: Less than you would expect. Collection, pagination and rate-limit cooldowns all run inside the extension and consume no host model quota — the extension hands back only structured results. Tokens go to three things: understanding the request, issuing calls and reading results, and the analysis and writing. It also reuses existing data before collecting anything new, and previews large payloads before paging into detail.

items.question: What is the difference between the skill and the MCP — do I set up both?
items.answer: One connector brings both. The MCP server exposes 40+ tools that fetch data from the platforms; the content research skill supplies 12 written methods that tell Doubao how to analyse and write once the data is back. Tools without methods give you data with no conclusion.

items.question: Do I still need the browser extension after connecting Doubao?
items.answer: Yes. The agent package cannot run on its own and does not replace the extension. Every page visit happens through the extension in your own browser, and the agent can only use capabilities you approved there.

items.question: Does my data pass through your servers?
items.answer: Collection runs in your own browser using the sessions you are already logged into; the session is never handed to the agent. Never paste cookies, tokens, activation codes or device keys into a conversation, issue or log — the agent will not ask for them. Revoking one agent's authorization leaves the others alone.

items.question: Could it collect things or spend credits on its own?
items.answer: No. Before any new collection it states the source, time range, volume, what it will read and the cost boundary, and waits for your agreement. Billable capabilities such as transcripts show an estimated credit cost and balance for a second confirmation. Silence is never treated as consent, and anything beyond the approved scope is asked again.

items.question: Is it free?
items.answer: The browser extension itself is free to use. Agent access requires an active membership, and billable capabilities such as video transcripts need credits plus a confirmation before they run. Analysis, generation and reporting on the agent side cost no MediaClaw credits.
